concept.name: Force index
concept.definition: Alexander Elder's oscillator (Trading for a Living) multiplying the close-to-close price change by volume, combining direction, extent, and participation into one measure of the force behind a move; the smoothed 13-period EMA form is the standard version.
concept.intuition: A one-point gain on huge volume shows more conviction than the same gain on a trickle - Force Index scores moves by both size and participation.
concept.mechanics: Force(1) = (Close_t - Close_{t-1}) x Volume_t; Force(13) = 13-period EMA of Force(1). Used for trend confirmation at the zero line, divergences, and - in Elder's pullback system - a 2-period Force Index against a 22-day EMA trend filter.
concept.formula: FI(1) = (Close_t - Close_{t-1}) x Volume_t; FI(13) = EMA(FI(1), 13).
concept.failure_modes: The raw 1-period version is extremely jagged and the smoothed version lags; because it is price change times volume in absolute terms, values are not comparable across securities.
concept.misconceptions: A positive Force Index does not mean buyers are 'in control' going forward - it records that the last bars rose on volume, which can reverse immediately.
concept.example: A close rising from 50.00 to 50.84 on 162,619 shares gives Force(1) = 0.84 x 162,619 ~ +136,600, the largest reading in StockCharts' Pfizer example.
